lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Targeted correction: selecting an efficient criterion

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: Each example contains the correction, not just the answer.

items.prompt: Two sides and the included angle are congruent. Which criterion?
Why is SSA not a congruence criterion?

steps: The swinging side can meet the ray at two points.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Before solving, say which error the problem is testing for.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. In triangle ABC, ∠A = 32° and ∠B = 44°. Find ∠F.
A rigid motion is a transformation that …
choices: preserves area but may change side lengths
preserves shape but may change size
maps every figure to a similar figure

items.prompt: In two triangles, all three pairs of corresponding sides are congruent. Which congruence criterion applies?
Two triangles share two pairs of congruent sides and a pair of congruent angles that are not between those sides. Why does this fail to prove congruence?
choices: The angle must be a right angle for any criterion to apply.
The triangles are congruent, but the criterion is simply named differently.
The unknown side can close the triangle in two different ways, producing one acute and one obtuse triangle from the same measurements.
Two sides are never enough information under any circumstances.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Triangle ABC is congruent to triangle DEF. In triangle ABC, ∠A = 37° and ∠B = 32°. Find ∠F.
If a sequence of rigid motions maps △ABC onto △DEF, then …
choices: only the corresponding sides are congruent
every pair of corresponding sides and angles is congruent
only the corresponding angles are congruent
the triangles have equal area but need not be congruent

items.prompt: In two triangles, the hypotenuses and one pair of legs of two right triangles are congruent. Which congruence criterion applies?
In two triangles, two pairs of corresponding angles and the pair of included sides are congruent. Which congruence criterion applies?
